newsitem.title: USA: Few concerns to cloud columbium's horizon.
newsitem.headline: Few concerns to cloud columbium's horizon.

text.p: Columbium buyers need not fear as there may be enough of the young metal to last a thousand years, and prices will barely fluctuate in the forseeable future, the world's leading producer said.
Known as niobium outside the United States, production is dominated by Brazil's Companhia Brasileira de Metalurgica e Mineracao, or CBMM.

"We don't see any reason to suspect that the pricing will vary much. Certainly no volatile fluctuations are predicted," Geoffrey Tither of Reference Metals Inc, part of CBMM, told Ryan's Notes vanadium, molybdenum and columbium conference.
Ferro-columbium prices have barely changed in the past 20 years, and are currently about $6.80 per pound of contained columbium.
Columbium is largely used in microalloyed steel for construction and autos.
World consumption was 16,000 to 17,000 tonnes last year, Tither estimated.

CBMM accounted for some 60 percent of the market, with Brazil's Mineracao Catalao de Goias with 15-20 percent, and Niobec in Canada, a joint venture between Teck and Cambior, with about 20 percent, Tither said.
Some eight percent of the world's steel output contains columbium. A growing application is in stainless steel for car exhausts, where columbium is used with titanium.
In the U.S. microalloyed steel accounts for 76.9 percent of columbium consumption, with stainless steel, 6.7 percent, niobium alloys 2.7 percent, and superalloys 13.1 percent.
U.S. columbium consumption last year was 5,000 tonnes.

CBMM's columbium reserves at its pyrochlore mine in Araxa, will last 500 years at current production rates, but mining is only done on the surface - the main deposit is underground and untouched, and could well last a thousand years in total, Tither said.
